sections.heading: C — Defensive driving, attention and fatigue
sections.markdown:
## C — Defensive driving, attention and fatigue

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A86
If not already in the exit-side lane, signal and move toward it about half a mile before the freeway exit. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A86
Signal before entering the deceleration lane, then slow there without disrupting freeway traffic flow. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A86
Adjust speed to any posted exit-ramp speed while traveling through the ramp. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A86
After leaving a freeway ramp, stay alert and adapt to the new road's conditions and slower speeds. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A86
Safe driving requires knowing and following road rules and proper procedures, with courtesy and consideration for others. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A86
Mental and physical condition can affect driving performance. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A86
Remain patient in heavy traffic, avoid hurried last-second decisions and rely on personal alertness rather than other drivers' signals. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A87
Before entering the vehicle, inspect both its front and rear for children or obstacles in its path. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A87
Before driving, adjust the seat and mirrors and fasten the safety belt. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A87
Check that passengers are seated and belted properly so they do not interfere with driving. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A87
For the handbook's starting routine, set the parking brake and verify Park or Neutral before starting the engine. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A87
Hold the foot brake and, when fitted, the clutch while selecting the proper starting gear; then release the parking brake before pulling out. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A87
The handbook's movement routine applies when leaving a curb, entering a parking space or changing lanes. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A87
Before leaving a curb, entering a parking space or changing lanes, check the mirrors first, then signal for five seconds or one hundred feet before moving. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A87
Before moving sideways, look over the shoulder in the intended direction. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A87
Move gradually and smoothly only when safe, then cancel the turn signal. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A88
If emotionally upset, have someone else drive. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A88
Worry, distraction and overconfidence can interfere with safe, alert driving. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A88
Concentrate on driving rather than daydreaming, shopping from the car, intense conversation or scenery. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A88
Give extra room to drivers entering from a driveway or intersection where buildings, fences, trees or vehicles block their view. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A88
Leave extra room for drivers backing from driveways or parking spaces. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A88
Allow extra room around a vehicle whose windows are covered by snow or ice because its driver may not see you. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A88
Allow extra room for potentially distracted delivery or construction workers and playing children. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A88
Give extra room to drivers conversing, tending children, navigating a complex intersection or looking for an address. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A89
If another driver is passing as a curve, hill or oncoming vehicle approaches, slow down and let that driver return to the lane promptly. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A89
Make space for a driver forced toward the lane by another car, pedestrian, cyclist, obstacle or lane reduction. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A89
For emergency readiness, the handbook recommends opposite-side steering-wheel hand positions near nine and three o'clock; use the owner's manual for proper placement in an airbag-equipped vehicle. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A89
Scan by moving the eyes and reading the road instead of maintaining a fixed stare ahead. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A89
Look roughly ten to fifteen seconds ahead; the handbook equates that to about a city block. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A89
Look both ways when approaching places where a vehicle, person or animal might cross the driving path. [A89]
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A90
Check rear traffic several times each minute to notice tailgating, fast-approaching vehicles or attempted passes. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A90
A blind spot is a rear-corner area on either side that mirrors do not show. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A90
Without a right-side mirror, the right blind spot is larger than the left one. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A90
Before a sideways maneuver, make a quick head check of the blind spot instead of relying only on mirrors. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A90
Avoid remaining in another driver's blind spot so that driver can see the vehicle. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A90
Identify potential hazards ahead, including vehicles, pedestrians, animals or situations that may require a speed or direction change. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A90
After identifying a hazard, predict what might happen and prepare for the worst plausible action, such as a playing child entering the road. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A90
Decide how to respond before danger becomes immediate, then act smoothly, predictably and soon enough to avoid a crash. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0090]

Misconceptions: Mirrors do not reveal every blind spot; energy drinks are not a reliable remedy for drowsy driving. Courtesy from another driver does not replace the driver's own observation.
Mnemonic: Identify, predict, decide and execute is the handbook's hazard-response order, presented as a learning cue.
Glossary: Blind spots are rear-corner areas outside mirror views; scanning means moving the eyes to read the road; highway hypnosis is drowsiness associated with monotonous driving.
Dynamic facts: present phone-law consequences, course availability and vehicle-specific instructions remain bounded by their actual official evidence.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page eighty-seven gives five seconds or one hundred feet for starting from a curb, entering a parking space or changing lanes without resolving which measure applies in each context. Other accepted source sections provide maneuver-specific timing. The procedure is covered, but this unqualified alternative is not taught as a universal timing rule; scope needs reconciliation.
The greater-than-ninety-percent driver-error assertion on physical page eighty-six has no study, date, denominator or causal method in the staged text. Withheld as an unverified statistic.

The concluding side-scanning instruction continues from physical page eighty-nine onto ninety with a warning that other drivers may run a light. The local complete side-scanning instruction is covered; the complete cross-page sentence and its rationale remain a binding-span debt.

The blind-spot illustration referenced on physical page ninety has not received semantic visual review. The text definition and shoulder-check rule are source-bound; graphic interpretation remains unresolved.
